Subject: Hosted API latency commitments and evidence request

Hi Marissa / Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week. As we scope our procurement checklist internally, Legal and SRE asked for clarified latency commitments for the Hosted API and an evidence package we can surface in our vendor review. Specifically we need:

- Concrete p50 and p95 latency targets for the Hosted API per region (US / EU) under the committed tier.
- How those percentiles are measured: sampling cadence, window size (rolling hours/days), aggregation method.
- Any carveouts or transient-exemption policies (maintenance, regional blackouts, large burst traffic).
- Runbook for when latency degrades: who we page, expected response times, fallback model behavior.

Can you send a short playbook and some telemetry screenshots or sample CSVs we can include in the questionnaire? We have an internal deadline of Nov 30 to finish vendor scoring.

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a quick call to clarify.

Bryan Wells
Director, Infrastructure & Platform
Altera Tech
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency commitments and evidence request

Bryan —

Thanks for the clear list. We're able to provide a compact SLO statement plus an evidence bundle that maps directly to each ask. High level summary below; I'll attach a short playbook and a small evidence ZIP in a follow-up email (or link if you prefer Drive).

Proposed SLO (Hosted API, committed tier, US region):
- p50: 70 ms median response latency (inference path excluding network egress).
- p95: 320 ms 95th percentile (measured over configured request types; latency defined as server-side request-enter to final-token-emitted).

Measurement & windowing: rolling 72-hour measurement window with 5-minute sampling buckets, aggregated hourly, then weighted by request volume across the epoch to avoid skew from cold-starts. We capture both raw per-request latencies and per-route summaries (by model and seq-length bin).

Carveouts / transient exceptions:
- Scheduled maintenance windows are carved out when announced with >=48h notice.
- Regional network blackouts: automatic regional carveout with post-mortem evidence if external provider outage confirmed.
- Burst traffic above the committed bursts (documented in the contract appendix) will be counted but flagged for mitigation; limited transient grace (up to two 1-hour windows per quarter) can be negotiated in exceptional onboarding periods.

Runbook / on-call:
- Primary SRE on-call (Redwood): paged within 5 minutes of p95 breach detection; response acknowledgement within 15 minutes and initial mitigation steps within 1 hour.
- Fallback policy: automatic routing to a lighter-weight quantized model variant for reads under 500 tokens; routing takes effect within 90s after automated detection.

Action items:
1) I'll upload a small evidence bundle (percentile export CSVs for a representative 30-day period, config snippets, and a screenshot of our console measurement page).
2) Kimberly, can you confirm the on-call contact matrix and escalation SLAs we should publish in the playbook?
3) Bryan, let me know if you need the EU numbers with identical windowing or prefer a separate regional baseline.

I'll follow up with attachments in an hour.

—Marissa
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference

- Playbook: "oncall-playbook-v1.pdf" contains the page/ack/escalation matrix, alert IDs, and our fallback flow with timing.
